summary: The 14-day telemetry analysis demonstrates exceptionally stable glucose control with a Time in Range (70-180 mg/dL) of 99.7%, average glucose of 117.0 mg/dL, low glycemic variability (CV 12.9%), and zero recorded time below 70 mg/dL. The active AAPS profile and meal bolus strategies are highly effective. Minor postprandial excursions during weekend brunch (peaks up to 188 mg/dL) resolve smoothly within 4 hours without causing late-phase hypoglycemia. Unreported AAPS activation and sensitivity raw flags should be verified directly in the smartphone application interface.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM data coverage is 100.0% across 14 days with 1,345 entries, a 15-minute sampling cadence, and no gaps exceeding 15 minutes. Authoritative active profile and treatment logs are complete.
analysis_steps.evidence: 1,345 valid entries, 28 carb treatments, 28 insulin treatments, 4 temp target entries, active profile 950d0da5-fd1d-4fdc-8a12-298fa1671fd1.

analysis_steps.findings: Outstanding glycemic safety with 0.0% Time Below 70 mg/dL, 99.7% Time in Range, and 0.3% Time Above 180 mg/dL. CV is low at 12.9%. Two brief, isolated overnight dips reaching 70-71 mg/dL occurred around 03:00 UTC on 2026-08-11 and 2026-08-17.
analysis_steps.evidence: Mean BG 117.0 mg/dL, SD 15.1 mg/dL, minimum BG 70 mg/dL, maximum BG 188 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of logged activity or sleep timing during early morning glucose dips.

analysis_steps.findings: Basal rates (0.85-1.05 U/h) and target ranges (90-115 mg/dL) effectively maintain fasting and inter-meal stability. The slight glucose drift around 02:00-03:00 local time is managed well by automated loop modulation.
analysis_steps.evidence: Hourly mean glucose ranges between 102.3 mg/dL and 119.9 mg/dL during non-meal hours.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Complete 5-minute temp basal rate logs to inspect exact loop attenuation depth overnight.

analysis_steps.findings: Carb ratios (9-12 g/U) and ISF segments (40-48 mg/dL/U) are well-calibrated. Postprandial glucose returns to baseline within 4 hours across all recurring meal types. DIA of 5.5 hours aligns with observed insulin action time.
analysis_steps.evidence: 240-minute postprandial glucose changes average -2 to +8 mg/dL for breakfast and -11 to +1 mg/dL for brunch.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB (3 min interval, 45 min max basal) and UAM (30 min max basal) are active and functioning as expected without causing insulin stacking or postprandial hypoglycemia.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Specific SMB activation condition flags are unpopulated (null) in Nightscout raw telemetry.

analysis_steps.findings: Safety limits (Max Basal 2.4 U/h, Max IOB 8.0 U) provide sufficient headroom for automated corrections while preventing runaway delivery. Dynamic ISF adjustment factor is at 100%.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Autosens and Dynamic Sensitivity enablement flags are unpopulated (null) in Nightscout raw settings.

analysis_steps.findings: Prebolus strategy (20 min for fast carbs, 10 min for mixed brunch) and immediate split ratios (60-70%) successfully match carbohydrate absorption profiles and avoid postprandial hypoglycemia.
analysis_steps.evidence: Weekday breakfast peaks at 157-167 mg/dL; weekend brunch peaks at 188 mg/dL, both clearing to start levels within 4 hours.

analysis_steps.findings: Declared e-carbs for weekend brunch (20g over 120 min) match observed extended absorption curves well. Active UAM safely assists with residual absorption.
analysis_steps.evidence: Extended absorption returns glucose smoothly to 111-115 mg/dL by 240 minutes post-meal.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: E-carb entries are declared in user context but not explicitly split into separate Nightscout carb records.

analysis_steps.findings: All findings across data quality, safety, profile parameters, automation settings, and meal strategies are coherent. The current basal, CR, ISF, and DIA profile should be maintained without changes. Unpopulated automation flags should be verified in AAPS preferences.
analysis_steps.evidence: TIR 99.7%, TBR 0.0%, average glucose 117.0 mg/dL across 14 days of complete telemetry.

strengths: Exceptional 99.7% Time in Range with zero recorded time below 70 mg/dL across 14 days.
Low glycemic variability (CV 12.9%, SD 15.1 mg/dL) indicating predictable insulin sensitivity and baseline stability.
Well-calibrated Carb Ratios (9-12 g/U) and ISF settings (40-48 mg/dL/U) allowing 4-hour postprandial return to baseline.
Effective meal bolus strategies including appropriate prebolus timing and split bolus ratios for fast versus mixed meals.
issues: Minor peak postprandial excursions during weekend brunch reaching 188 mg/dL (7.1% time above range in that specific hourly window).
Unpopulated raw settings flags in Nightscout for Autosens and SMB activation conditions.

recommendations.title: Verify Unpopulated AAPS Settings in Application Preferences
recommendations.description: Several automation flags (such as SMB activation conditions and Autosens enablement) appear as null in Nightscout telemetry. Confirm directly in the AAPS user interface that these settings match your intended configuration.

recommendations.title: Maintain Current Carb Ratios and Monitor Weekend Brunch Excursions
recommendations.description: Current Carb Ratios provide excellent 4-hour recovery. For weekend brunch, consider extending the prebolus timing from 10 minutes to 15 minutes before adjusting Carb Ratios.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep all current profile settings (basal rates, CR, ISF, target ranges, and DIA) unchanged.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Current settings achieve 99.7% Time in Range, 0.0% Time Below Range, and a low 12.9% Coefficient of Variation across 14 days of complete telemetry.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Perform a standard 14-day review or evaluate bedtime-to-overnight stability if early morning dips reoccur.

parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=45 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=30 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=45 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=30 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: Delivery frequency and basal minute caps are appropriate for oref1 dynamic corrections.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Max basal (2.4 U/h) and Max IOB (8 U) provide appropriate safety boundaries given total daily dose of ~10.2 U.
Autosens enablement status is unpopulated in telemetry; verify settings in AAPS preferences.
Carbohydrate absorption parameters match observed postprandial glucose recovery dynamics.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Administer a 15-20 minute prebolus for standard meals with a 70% immediate bolus split, relying on active SMB and UAM automation to manage residual absorption.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Keeps postprandial peak spikes under 170 mg/dL for standard meals and returns glucose to baseline within 4 hours without hypoglycemia.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Observe whether increasing prebolus time from 10 to 15 minutes for weekend brunch reduces the 2-hour peak below 160 mg/dL.

exceptions.suggestion: Use a 10-15 minute prebolus with a 60% immediate bolus split and declare 20g e-carbs over 120 minutes with a 15-minute start offset.
exceptions.rationale: Provides extended coverage matching slower fat/protein carbohydrate absorption, preventing late postprandial rise.

implementation_steps: Review current telemetry results with your diabetes care team.
Maintain all active profile parameters (basal, CR, ISF, DIA, and targets) as currently configured.
Verify unpopulated AAPS preference flags (SMB activation conditions and Autosens settings) directly in your smartphone application.
For weekend brunch, test extending prebolus timing from 10 to 15 minutes while maintaining current e-carb declarations to reduce peak postprandial rise.
education: Time in Range of 99.7% with 0.0% time below 70 mg/dL reflects optimal basal and bolus calibration.
A Coefficient of Variation (CV) below 36% indicates stable and predictable glucose control.
Prebolus timing helps align insulin peak activity with carbohydrate absorption, reducing initial postprandial spikes without increasing total insulin dosage.
safety_notes: This analysis is for decision-support purposes only and does not constitute medical advice.
Always make therapy changes one parameter at a time and consult your healthcare provider before modifying insulin delivery settings.
Monitor blood glucose closely following any changes to bolus timing or meal strategies.
